title: Per-day reveal sequence: entrance animation, extra confetti burst, and romantic 3D reveal effects

requirements.summary: Run a one-time-per-screen-open day reveal animation sequence when viewing an unlocked day in DayDetailScreen; never run it for locked days.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening an unlocked day in the Day Detail view triggers a reveal animation automatically without additional clicks.
Opening a locked day does not trigger the reveal animation sequence.
Navigating away and back to the same unlocked day triggers the reveal again (i.e., it is tied to opening the day screen, not a global one-time flag).
All user-facing text remains in English (no new non-English strings introduced).

file_operations.description: Add a mount-triggered reveal sequence that only activates when the day is unlocked (e.g., local state keyed by dayNumber/view entry) and applies entrance/reveal animation classes to the day content container; ensure locked-day rendering path does not start the sequence.
Add CSS keyframes/utility classes for the DayDetail reveal entrance (e.g., fade/slide/scale) and ensure they respect prefers-reduced-motion (reduced/disabled motion while keeping layout usable).
Create a small hook to detect prefers-reduced-motion (matchMedia) so DayDetailScreen and reveal effects can gracefully reduce/disable animations when requested.

requirements.summary: Add a time-bounded, denser extra-confetti burst on unlocked day open, without blocking interaction or causing performance issues.
acceptanceCriteria: On opening an unlocked day, the confetti burst is visibly denser than the existing medium confetti effect.
The burst ends automatically after a short duration and does not continue indefinitely.
The confetti overlay does not block interaction with the Day Detail screen (pointer events remain unaffected).
No noticeable performance degradation occurs after repeatedly opening multiple days.

file_operations.description: Extend confetti support to include a time-bounded "burst" mode/trigger (separate from existing continuous medium confetti): generate a denser set of pieces on trigger, automatically clear them after a short duration, and keep pointer-events disabled for the overlay.

Wire the new extra-confetti burst to the unlocked day reveal sequence (trigger on screen open for unlocked days only) while keeping the existing medium confetti behavior intact; ensure repeated navigations re-trigger the burst and that it does not run for locked days.

If needed for the denser burst, add/adjust confetti animation utilities to keep the burst short-lived and performant (e.g., ensure animations finish and elements can be removed cleanly), while preserving prefers-reduced-motion behavior.

requirements.summary: Add romantic celebratory 3D animations (e.g., flowers/gift boxes) as part of the unlocked day reveal sequence, layered so the main message remains readable and reduced-motion is respected.
acceptanceCriteria: On opening an unlocked day, at least one clearly 3D animated romantic element (e.g., flower(s), gift box(es)) appears as part of the reveal sequence.
The 3D effect is visually distinct from the existing 2D RomanticScene particle canvas (i.e., not just more 2D particles).
The 3D animations do not prevent the user from reading the day message; content remains legible and accessible.
If the user has prefers-reduced-motion enabled, the reveal animations are reduced/disabled gracefully (no aggressive motion), while the page remains fully usable.

file_operations.description: Create a lightweight 3D-effect overlay component (CSS perspective/transforms) that renders romantic elements like a gift box and/or flowers with celebratory motion during the reveal; ensure it is pointer-events-none and visually subtle so it does not obscure the message.

Mount Romantic3DReveal only for unlocked days and only during the day reveal sequence; place it in the visual stack so the day content stays legible (e.g., behind the Card content or at low opacity around edges) and disable/reduce it when prefers-reduced-motion is enabled (using the new hook).

Add the required CSS keyframes/classes for the 3D reveal effects (e.g., rotateY/rotateX, pop-in, gentle drift) and ensure reduced-motion rules prevent aggressive motion while keeping the UI fully usable.
